blocks.heading: The duplicate-work problem
blocks.body: Two workers can observe the same missing job and both begin it. A short-lived Redis key lets one worker claim the job before the other starts.

blocks.caption: Only one worker receives the lock token.

steps.text: The worker creates a random token.
Redis stores the token only when the key is absent.
The worker releases the key only when its token matches.

lines.cmd: redis-cli SET job:42 token NX EX 30
redis-cli SET job:42 other NX EX 30

blocks.ask: Why must the release operation compare the token before deleting the key?
rubric: It prevents a delayed worker from deleting a newer owner's lock.
The token identifies the lease owner.
The comparison and deletion must be atomic.

blocks.ask: Write the guarded release operation for the lock token.
blocks.starter:
if redis.call('get', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then
  -- release here
end

blocks.situation: When a worker must claim a missing lock for thirty seconds, type the command.

blocks.ask: What does NX protect in the lock acquisition command?

options.text: It writes only when the key does not already exist.
It renews the key every time a worker reads it.
options.why: NX controls creation, not renewal or reads.

options.text: It deletes the key after the expiry period.
options.why: EX supplies expiry; NX does not delete keys.
